angle: Before you give AI the keys to your desktop, install better locks: scopes, logs, and kill switches.
sourceTitle: Meta’s Muse hits Mac, letting the AI take actions on your computer
linkedinPost:
AI is getting hands—not just a mouth.

TechCrunch covers Meta’s Muse on Mac: an agent that can act across your files and apps. Powerful idea. Also a governance nightmare if you roll it into the enterprise without controls.

From the FDE seat, we treat “action-taking agents” like new employees with probation badges. They get minimal access, everything is logged, and there’s a visible emergency stop.

If you’re piloting desktop agents, ship these guardrails on day one:
- Least-privilege scopes tied to business tasks, not apps.
- Human-in-the-loop for irreversible actions; batch the rest.
- Full audit trails (who/what/when/why) with easy review.
- A big red kill switch that any user can hit.

Agents that can click, send, and move files will create value. But the first outage or rogue action will end your program faster than any security review.

What’s your “locks before keys” checklist for agentic pilots? #AIAdoption #EnterpriseAI #CustomerExperience
